rows.title: The whole view
rows.text: If you are a pond slider, you have four kinds of color-sensing cone, one of them for ultraviolet, and a review estimates from the cells in your retina that you see about a fifth of the detail a human sees. Sharpness has been measured in only a few other species, including the green anole, the brown anole, the box turtle and the common watersnake, and nobody has measured it in most lizards, snakes and turtles. Nobody has measured how far around you can see, and pupil shape is known for only a few species, such as the round pupils of the painted turtle and the garter snake.
rows.note: Replaced "reports" with "estimates". No record gives field of view for any reptile, so the row says so. The ultraviolet cone is stated only for the pond slider.
